title: Many Copies, Acting as One — Arche
description: Herlihy and Wing's linearizability: three trading houses on the ring road ask that orders be filled as though one keeper had entered them all on one board, in the sequence they really came by the sun.
question: When data is kept in several copies, what does it take for them to act as one? And who could ever tell the difference?
how: We find out by exploring how three ancient Greek trading houses filled one another's orders in the sequence they really came, though none of them could read the hour.

papers.authors: Maurice P. Herlihy and Jeannette M. Wing
papers.title: Linearizability: A Correctness Condition for Concurrent Objects
